rows.note: This is the everyday Hong Kong construction verb for coating a wall or other surface with plaster.

example.english: We need to plaster the whole wall tomorrow, and only then can we paint it.
example.traditional: 我哋聽日要幫成幅牆批灰，之後先可以髹油。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 ting1 jat6 jiu3 bong1 sing4 fuk1 coeng4 pai1 fui1 zi1 hau6 sin1 ho2 ji5 jau1 jau4

rows.note: This is the everyday all-purpose term for a small sticking plaster.

example.english: You’ve cut your finger; just put on a plaster.
example.traditional: 你個手指損咗，貼塊膠布就得喇。
example.jyutping: nei5 go3 sau2 zi2 syun2 zo2 tip3 faai3 gaau1 bou3 zau6 dak1 laa3

rows.note: Use this when something is covered all over with posters, advertisements, or other items, rather than coated with building plaster.

example.english: The posters plaster the whole wall, so you can’t even see the wall from a distance.
example.traditional: 啲海報貼滿晒成幅牆，遠望連牆身都睇唔到。
example.jyutping: di1 hoi2 bou3 tip3 mun5 saai3 seng4 fuk1 coeng4 jyun5 mong6 lin4 coeng4 san1 dou1 tai2 m4 dou2

rows.note: Use this for a medicinal paste applied to the skin, rather than for a bandage or a cast.

example.english: Apply this plaster to the mosquito bite and it’ll soon stop itching.
example.traditional: 呢隻藥膏搽喺蚊叮嗰度，好快就冇咁痕。
example.jyutping: ne1 zek3 joek6 gou1 caa4 hai2 man1 deng1 go2 dou6 hou2 faai3 zau6 mou5 gam3 han4

rows.note: In a medical context, this commonly refers to the plaster cast put on an injured limb.

example.english: The doctor said I need a plaster so my leg can heal properly.
example.traditional: 醫生話要打石膏，隻腳先可以慢慢好返。
example.jyutping: ji1 saang1 waa6 jiu3 daa2 sek6 gou1 zek3 goek3 sin1 ho2 ji5 maan6 maan6 hou2 faan1
